ui.lead: Each icon sits on the kind of orbit its mission uses. Low Earth orbit is the inner ring, then medium, geostationary, and a long ellipse for highly elliptical orbits. Every ring stays visible. Nothing here is a live position.
ui.scale: The ring order follows NASA Earth Observatory’s Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits and the Earth-centered style of NASA Eyes on the Earth. Imagery: NASA Visible Earth / Blue Marble Next Generation. Created by the Founder and SI. Sun: NASA/SDO AIA 304. Moon: NASA/Goddard/Arizona State University, LROC WAC.
ui.helpsPage: The sentence above is the mission page on this site. We do not add a broader claim than that page.
ui.explain1: A Lagrange point is a place where the gravity of the Sun and the Earth lines up with the motion of an orbit, so a spacecraft can keep pace with Earth. NASA says the pull of the two large masses equals the centripetal force a small object needs to move with them. There are five. L1, L2, and L3 sit on the Sun–Earth line and are unstable. L4 leads Earth and L5 follows, at the tips of equilateral triangles, and those two are stable.
ui.explain2: L1 and L2 are each about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. NASA’s Webb orbit page rounds that to 1 million miles, which is about 930,000 miles if you convert 1.5 million kilometers directly. L1 faces the Sun, so SOHO and DSCOVR get a steady view of it. L2 is on the night side, a cold and steady spot for telescopes such as Webb, Euclid, and Roman. A spacecraft does not sit on the point. It loops around the point in a halo or Lissajous orbit.
ui.explain3: Webb’s trip started with launch on an Ariane 5 on 25 December 2021. NASA says that launch put Webb on a transfer path of about 30 days. Three mid-course correction burns refined the path, and the last one, on 24 January 2022, pointed Webb into its halo orbit. Because L1, L2, and L3 are unstable, Webb fires small station-keeping burns, on average about every 42 days, or it would drift away. L4 and L5 do not need that kind of care. L3 stays hidden behind the Sun, about 1 AU from the Sun and about 2 AU from Earth. L4 and L5 are about 1 AU from Earth, 60 degrees ahead and behind. NASA’s Moon fact sheet lists a mean distance of 384,400 km (238,855 miles).
ui.dL12: about 1.5 million km · about 1 million miles
ui.dL3: about 2 AU from Earth · far side of the Sun

The first space telescope specifically designed to detect asteroids and comets that may be potential hazards to Earth: a single telescope about 50 cm (almost 20 inches) across, seeing in two heat-sensing infrared wavelengths.
Launch no earlier than September 2027, on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Florida.

sats.name: Europa Clipper
sats.does: NASA's Europa Clipper is on its way to Jupiter's ocean moon, with an Earth gravity assist on December 3, 2026 and 49 close Europa flybys from 2030.
sats.helps: The mission page says it is on the way to Jupiter’s ocean moon, with an Earth gravity assist on 3 December 2026 and close Europa flybys from 2030. It studies another ocean world, not Earth’s oceans.
sats.credit: Photo: NASA (PIA25125). Europa Clipper during assembly.
brief: Europa Clipper (NASA) NASA's Europa Clipper is on its way to Jupiter's ocean moon, with an Earth gravity assist on December 3, 2026 and 49 close Europa flybys from 2030.
An orbiter that will make 49 close flybys of Europa to study its ice shell, ocean and chemistry.
Launched October 14, 2024; Earth gravity-assist flyby December 3, 2026; arrives at Jupiter in April 2030.
Jupiter's icy moon Europa, about 1.8 billion miles of travel from Earth.

sats.name: Juice
sats.does: ESA's Juice will study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, with 35 moon flybys after it reaches Jupiter in July 2031. Cruising.
sats.helps: The mission page says Juice is cruising and will study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa after reaching Jupiter in July 2031. That is comparative planetology, not an Earth forecast.
sats.credit: Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech (PIA24026). Juice’s RIME radar.
brief: Juice (ESA) ESA's Juice will study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, with 35 moon flybys after it reaches Jupiter in July 2031.
September 2026 Earth flyby complete; next Earth flyby January 2029.
A spacecraft with 85 square metres of solar wings and ten instruments, studying Jupiter and three ocean-bearing moons.
Launched April 14, 2023 on Ariane 5; Earth flybys September 2026 (done) and January 2029; arrival July 2031.

sats.name: Psyche
sats.does: NASA's Psyche used a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 to head for a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029, to learn what a planet's core is like.
sats.helps: The mission page says a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 sent Psyche toward a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029, to learn what a planet’s core can be like.
sats.credit: Photo: NASA. Psyche spacecraft at Astrotech.
brief: Psyche (NASA) NASA's Psyche used a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 to head for a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029 (NASA).
NASA, with the mission led by Arizona State University and managed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
An orbiter that will map asteroid Psyche, which may be the partial metal core of an early planet building block.
Launched 13 October 2023; Mars flyby 15 May 2026; arrival August 2029.

sats.name: Hera
sats.does: ESA's Hera arrives at the asteroid Dimorphos in November 2026 to measure what NASA's DART impact did, turning deflection into a repeatable defense.
sats.helps: The mission page says Hera arrives at Dimorphos in November 2026 to measure what NASA’s DART impact did. That is a planetary-defense measurement, and the arrival date is the one the page states.
sats.credit: Artist's concept (ESA – Science Office, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO).
brief: Hera Crash scene investigators for the first asteroid humans ever moved.
The European Space Agency, through its Space Safety programme, working with NASA under the international AIDA collaboration.
A small, van-sized deep-space spacecraft that will perform a close-up "crash scene investigation" of Dimorphos, measuring its mass, its shifted orbit and DART's impact crater.
Juventas will make the first radar sounding inside an asteroid.
